name: Malta
headline_status: Adults in Malta may possess small amounts, grow four plants at home and join licensed non-profit cannabis clubs, but there are no commercial shops.
summary: In December 2021 Malta became the first EU country to legalise personal cannabis, through the Authority on the Responsible Use of Cannabis Act. Adults may carry up to 7 g, keep up to 50 g at home and grow four plants out of public view. Supply is limited to licensed non-profit associations for registered members, overseen by the Authority for the Responsible Use of Cannabis. Smoking in public and near children brings fines.

adult_use_since.value: 18 December 2021, under Act LXVI of 2021, which created the Authority on the Responsible Use of Cannabis and amended the drug laws.

possession_limit.value: Adults 18+ may carry up to 7 g without committing an offence and keep up to 50 g of dried cannabis at their registered home address. Carrying more than 7 g but no more than 28 g brings a €50–€100 penalty before a Commissioner for Justice.

home_grow.value: Up to 4 plants per registered residential address, however many adults live there, kept out of public view, without causing odour nuisance and out of reach of minors; breaching those conditions brings a €300–€500 penalty.

purchase_age.value: 18 for possession and for membership of a cannabis association.

public_use.value: Consuming cannabis in a public place, a place open to the public or where the smell causes a nuisance is fined €235; consuming it in front of a minor, in public or private, is fined €300–€500.

retail_sales.value: No shops. Licensed non-profit cannabis harm reduction associations (up to 500 members, all Maltese residents aged 18+) may supply each member no more than 7 g a day and 50 g a month.

regulator.value: Authority on the Responsible Use of Cannabis (ARUC), set up under Chapter 628 of the Laws of Malta, which registers and licenses associations.

penalties.value: Trafficking and supply remain criminal offences. A person habitually resident in Malta who is convicted a second time within two years for personal-use possession is ordered to appear before the Drug Offenders Rehabilitation Board.

tourists.value: Visitors cannot buy legally: tourists may not join cannabis associations, which require a Maltese ID card or residence card, and there are no shops. Importing cannabis remains illegal unless authorised for medical use.

timeline.event: Act LXVI of 2021 (Authority on the Responsible Use of Cannabis Act) takes effect, legalising personal possession and home growing

faq.a: Yes for adults within limits: 7 g in public, 50 g at home and four plants. There are no shops, only licensed non-profit clubs for residents.

faq.q: Can tourists buy cannabis in Malta?
faq.a: No. Cannabis associations serve registered residents only, and bringing cannabis into Malta can lead to criminal charges.

faq.q: Can you smoke weed in public in Malta?
faq.a: No. Public smoking is fined €235, and smoking in front of children €300 to €500.

sources.name: Laws of Malta – Chapter 628, Authority on the Responsible Use of Cannabis Act
Laws of Malta – Chapter 537, Drug Dependence (Treatment not Imprisonment) Act

changelog.note: Replaced secondary sources with Laws of Malta (Cap. 628, Cap. 537) and ARUC; added the €50–€100 penalty for 7–28 g and corrected the repeat-offence rule (Drug Offenders Rehabilitation Board)
